notes: Every statement the LLM may trigger. Params are named; :si (snapshot index) is injected by the engine.

rates.description: Current rates/APR/APY/dividends for loans, mortgages, certificates, checking, savings, money market.

keywords.description: Product-name words only, as they appear in the product label (e.g. ['30','year'], ['money','market'], ['84','month']). NEVER rate values or phrases from the question; omit if unsure.

amount.description: Dollar amount if the question gives one (balance or loan size).

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD, only if the question asks about a past date (e.g. 'as of May 2026' -> 2026-05-31). Omit otherwise.

rates.sql:
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT r.url, r.family, r.label, r.head, r.eff, r.rate, r.apr, r.apy, r.minearn, r.rank, r.hay, r.lo, r.hi, r.yr_lo, r.yr_hi,
         (SELECT group_concat(DISTINCT x.url) FROM rates x WHERE x.snap_idx=r.snap_idx AND x.ckey=r.ckey AND x.rank<=3
            AND x.rate IS r.rate AND x.apr IS r.apr AND x.apy IS r.apy) AS also,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.ckey ORDER BY (r.rank>1), COALESCE(NULLIF(r.eff,''),'0000') DESC, r.rank) AS rn
  FROM rates r WHERE r.snap_idx=:si AND r.family=:family AND r.segment=:segment)
 WHERE rn=1 AND (:amount IS NULL OR lo IS NULL OR (:amount>=lo AND :amount<=hi))
   AND (:model_year IS NULL OR yr_lo IS NULL OR (:model_year>=yr_lo AND :model_year<=yr_hi)) {kw}
 ORDER BY label LIMIT 40

credit_cards.description: Dupaco credit cards: names, APR ranges, intro offers.

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD, only if the question asks about a past date (e.g. 'as of May 2026' -> 2026-05-31). Omit otherwise.

credit_cards.sql: SELECT url, name, lo AS apr_lo, hi AS apr_hi, intro, intro_text FROM cards WHERE snap_idx=:si ORDER BY rank LIMIT 12

branch_hours.description: Lobby/drive-up hours, waterfall by source: first official-site passages (tier official), then hours listed in newsroom releases (older, per release date). Use for hours, comparing branches, or a named branch. Newsroom rows are DISTINCT schedules (same lines merged): first_pub..pub is the date range, n the number of announcements, title names the branches/events.

place.description: Branch/city/place name, e.g. 'Hy-Vee', 'Dubuque'. Empty for all.

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD, only if the question asks about a past date (e.g. 'as of May 2026' -> 2026-05-31). Omit otherwise.

branch_hours.sql:
SELECT * FROM (SELECT s.url, s.title, s.pub, s.rank, 'official-text' AS kind, substr(s.text,1,300) AS lines, '' AS first_pub, 1 AS n, '' AS also FROM sent s
   WHERE s.rank<=2 AND s.first_idx<=:si AND s.last_idx>=:si AND (s.text LIKE '%a.m.%' OR s.text LIKE '%p.m.%') AND (s.text LIKE '%Monday%' OR s.text LIKE '%obby%' OR s.text LIKE '%rive-up%' OR s.text LIKE '%rive up%')
   AND (:place='' OR s.text LIKE '%'||:place||'%' OR s.head LIKE '%'||:place||'%') ORDER BY s.rank, s.pub DESC LIMIT 6)
 UNION ALL
 SELECT * FROM (SELECT substr(MAX(h.pub||'|'||h.url),12) AS url, substr(group_concat(DISTINCT substr(h.title,1,70)),1,200) AS title, MAX(h.pub) AS pub, 4 AS rank, h.kind,
   replace(replace(h.lines,'\u2013','-'),char(8211),'-') AS lines, MIN(h.pub) AS first_pub, COUNT(*) AS n, group_concat(DISTINCT h.url) AS also FROM hours h WHERE h.snap_idx=:si
   AND (h.pub='' OR h.pub<=:asof) AND (:place='' OR h.title LIKE '%'||:place||'%' OR h.blurb LIKE '%'||:place||'%')
   GROUP BY h.kind, replace(replace(h.lines,'\u2013','-'),char(8211),'-') ORDER BY pub DESC LIMIT 16)

branch_locations.description: Branch/ATM addresses and services from the locator.

place.description: Street, city or name fragment. Empty for all.

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD, only if the question asks about a past date (e.g. 'as of May 2026' -> 2026-05-31). Omit otherwise.

branch_locations.sql:
SELECT url, name, kind, street, city, state, zip, services FROM locator WHERE snap_idx=:si
  AND (:place='' OR name LIKE '%'||:place||'%' OR street LIKE '%'||:place||'%' OR city LIKE '%'||:place||'%') LIMIT 25

branch_count.description: How many branch office locations Dupaco has: one row per distinct count reported, with the date of its newest report; the row marked newest is the current count.

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD, only if the question asks about a past date (e.g. 'as of May 2026' -> 2026-05-31). Omit otherwise.

branch_count.sql: SELECT url, pub, branch_count, CASE WHEN rn=1 THEN 'newest report' END AS note FROM (SELECT url, pub, value AS branch_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY pub DESC, value DESC) AS rn, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY value ORDER BY pub DESC) AS vr FROM counts WHERE snap_idx=:si) WHERE vr=1 ORDER BY pub DESC LIMIT 6

links.description: Find the official PAGE for a topic (where to see rates/info, how to join/apply, locator, forms). Rows: page_url = the page to give for 'see/find' questions; example_link = an application/action link on it (give it for 'join/apply/open'). Topic = ONE word, e.g. 'certificate', 'join', 'locator'. link_texts = the matching link labels on that page (evidence the page covers the topic). Rows are ranked best first: the first page_url is the page that covers the topic.

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD, only if the question asks about a past date (e.g. 'as of May 2026' -> 2026-05-31). Omit otherwise.

links.sql:
SELECT l.url AS page_url, p.title, COUNT(*) AS matches, MIN(l.href) AS example_link, substr(group_concat(DISTINCT substr(l.text,1,60)),1,220) AS link_texts FROM links l
  JOIN pages p ON p.snap_idx=l.snap_idx AND p.url=l.url
  WHERE l.snap_idx=:si AND p.rank<=3 AND (l.text LIKE '%'||:topic||'%' OR l.href LIKE '%'||:topic||'%' OR p.title LIKE '%'||:topic||'%')
  GROUP BY l.url ORDER BY (l.url LIKE '%business%'), p.rank, matches DESC LIMIT 8

search_text.description: Full-text passage search of the website. Use for anything else: routing number, closures, membership eligibility, fees, phone numbers, policies. Query words must match the page wording, so add synonyms of the action (e.g. update -> change, review, correct; contact information -> personal information, address, phone). The result also lists the section headings of the best pages (one row each), so facts that sit next to the matched passage are visible.

query.description: 2-4 distinctive keywords the answering page would contain (no 'Dupaco'), e.g. 'eligible join charter', 'Hy-Vee branch close'. May call up to 3 times with different queries.

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD, only if the question asks about a past date (e.g. 'as of May 2026' -> 2026-05-31). Omit otherwise.

search_text.sql:
SELECT s.id, s.url, s.rank, s.pub, s.head, substr(s.text,1,500) AS text FROM sent_fts f JOIN sent s ON s.id=f.rowid
  WHERE sent_fts MATCH :match AND s.first_idx<=:si AND s.last_idx>=:si ORDER BY bm25(sent_fts)+0.4*s.rank LIMIT 15
search_text.outline_sql: SELECT MIN(id) AS id, url, MIN(rank) AS rank, MAX(pub) AS pub, head, substr(group_concat(text, ' '), 1, 300) AS text FROM sent WHERE url=:u AND rank<=3 AND head<>'' AND first_idx<=:si AND last_idx>=:si GROUP BY head ORDER BY MIN(id) LIMIT 14

rate_lookup.description: Search rates by CRITERIA: which products/tiers pay a given rate (e.g. 'does any tier pay 0.35%'), the highest or lowest rate, rates at or above/below a value, or the tier for a dollar amount. Returns one summary row per product (min and max rate, tier where the max applies, how many tiers match) plus the matching tier rows. Name `product` when the question is about the tiers of one product (savings tiers -> Share Savings); omit it to search the whole family. Use `rates` instead for a plain 'what is the rate on X' lookup.

product.description: Product name as in the label, e.g. 'Share Savings', 'Health Savings Account', 'Money Market'. Omit to search every product of the family. For a question about 'savings tiers' / 'the savings account' use the family's main product (Share Savings).

apy_eq.description: Rate the question asks about, e.g. 0.35. Matches tiers whose APY (or rate) equals it.

apy_min.description: Only tiers at or above this rate.

apy_max.description: Only tiers at or below this rate.

amount.description: Dollar balance/loan size: only tiers that cover it.

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD, only if the question asks about a past date (e.g. 'as of May 2026' -> 2026-05-31). Omit otherwise.

rate_lookup.sql:
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT r.url, r.family, r.label, r.eff, r.rate, r.apr, r.apy, r.lo, r.hi, r.rank,
         (SELECT group_concat(DISTINCT x.url) FROM rates x WHERE x.snap_idx=r.snap_idx AND x.ckey=r.ckey AND x.rank<=3
            AND x.rate IS r.rate AND x.apr IS r.apr AND x.apy IS r.apy) AS also,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.ckey ORDER BY (r.rank>1), COALESCE(NULLIF(r.eff,''),'0000') DESC, r.rank) AS rn
  FROM rates r WHERE r.snap_idx=:si AND r.family=:family AND r.segment=:segment)
 WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY label LIMIT 300
